component.name: NanoTorrent
component.summary: A tiny, hackable Rust BitTorrent client based on PicoTorrent

description.p: NanoTorrent is a small BitTorrent client: a Rust port of PicoTorrent by Viktor Elofsson, built on librqbit.
Features:

ul.li: DHT, UDP trackers and MSE/PE protocol encryption.
Add several torrents at once, choosing which files to fetch from each.
Create torrents in BitTorrent v1, v2 or hybrid format.
Labels, and filters written in a small query language.
Per-torrent details: files, peers with country flags, and trackers by announce tier.
An optional authenticated HTTPS web interface for controlling it remotely.
Available in over 76 languages, switchable without restarting.

description.p: In the Add dialog, a folder has a checkbox of its own that ticks or unticks everything inside it, and All and None buttons tick or untick the whole torrent - no more unticking hundreds of files one at a time.
An optional qBittorrent-compatible web API lets Sonarr, Radarr and other tools made for qBittorrent control NanoTorrent.
The Seeds and Peers columns show the size of the swarm, file priorities survive pausing a torrent and land on the right file in hybrid torrents, and the web interface gets a security fix.

Double-clicking a .torrent file in the Finder on macOS opens it in NanoTorrent, instead of an error saying the file type cannot be opened. Magnet links clicked in a browser on macOS work the same way.

The amount uploaded for each torrent is kept when NanoTorrent closes; uploads not yet saved used to be lost on every exit. Peers that connect without encryption are accepted again - every one of them was being turned away.

Run without a window with nanotorrent --headless, on all three platforms. The limits on active torrents now apply in that mode too, and closing NanoTorrent saves the state of every torrent on the way out.

Fixes a window that came back partly drawn after being minimised for a long time on Windows. The GeoIP download now goes through your proxy, and importing from qBittorrent brings over base32 and BitTorrent v2 magnet links.

Security fix: the HTTPS web interface was open to a denial of service before login. A ratio limit now stops a torrent at the ratio it shows, and the AppImage starts on systems without libxkbcommon-x11.
A magnet link opens the Add dialog at once and fetches its metadata while the dialog is up, instead of waiting for it first. Portable mode gets a switch: nanotorrent --portable.
A hybrid torrent's Trackers tab shows both of its swarms, the Pieces bar is a map of the torrent, and NanoTorrent can take over from another client. Rendering no longer uses the graphics card.
Your share ratio no longer resets on restart. Trackers are announced by tier, removing a torrent asks first, more video players are recognised, and the web interface catches up with the desktop.
76 languages, up from 41. Stream a file to a media player while it downloads, and fold folders in the file lists. Finished and paused torrents no longer keep their files locked.
Magnet links go through the Add dialog like .torrent files, and a torrent with several files is saved into a folder of its own instead of spilling into the save path.
Drawing moved from the graphics card to the processor, lowering CPU and memory use.

Fixes paused torrents re-creating their files on startup. A torrent whose data had been deleted or moved could come back at 0% with a folder of empty files; nothing is written to disk now until a torrent actually starts.

The web interface receives live updates instead of polling, showing a connection indicator that reconnects on its own and the number of connected clients. Its torrent list can be paged and sorted across every page.

Preferences is rebuilt to match the main window, with icon tabs that scroll when they do not fit, and now shows the chosen language. The details panel fills as soon as you click, behind a loading overlay. Closing a window now really closes it.

Strict network mode: when a VPN interface or a SOCKS proxy is set, NanoTorrent switches off whatever that cannot cover — DHT, uTP, local peer discovery and UPnP — refuses to start if the interface is missing, and pauses everything if it disappears while running. Binding to an interface now works on Windows.
Security fix: a malicious .torrent whose filename carried a drive prefix could write outside the download folder on Windows.

The web interface gains the desktop toolbar, speed charts, resizable columns, multi-select, drag-and-drop adding, a configurable login lockout, and plugin control. Fixes dialogs that could open taller than the screen.
Plugins can reach the network, keep their own data, and open a window and a menu of their own. Includes an RSS feed reader as a plugin. Adds live download and upload charts to the toolbar.

Adds the plugin host: optional Rhai scripts that watch torrents and drive them, each declaring what it may reach and running only once approved. Plugins are off by default. Finishes desktop notifications on all three platforms.
BitTorrent v2 (BEP 52) and hybrid torrents, including v2 magnets. Adds the fast extension (BEP 6), upload-only (BEP 21), and per-tracker announce statistics.
Set a torrent's save path without moving its files, for data relocated outside the app. Fixes a burst of download-complete notifications when starting with completed torrents.

Adds a resizable details panel with per-version info hashes, advanced HTTP tuning and login rate limiting for the web interface, and completes the translations for all 41 languages. Fixes a progress bar that could read 100% before a torrent had finished, and a durability bug that could lose verified pieces after an unclean exit.
A Linux release.

ul.li: Opening a torrent's download folder opened the parent directory instead, and reported nothing when it failed
The window icon fell back to a generic one on Wayland
The notification-area icon could not be created in sandboxed environments

description.p: Fixes a crash on startup: turning off the notification-area icon made the application fail to launch every time afterwards, with no way to undo it from the interface.
The "Skip 'Add torrent' dialog" preference now works - it was stored but never acted on.
Batch torrent adding in both the desktop and web interfaces, a low-disk guard, and fixes for two bugs in session persistence.
